column1: # Deliberate differences from Yomitan d3c54c1 (docs/languages.md 8.2), read by tools/check-yomitan.mjs.

column7: The pack strips accents only from a lower-case single word. Yomitan also strips them from a capitalised word, which then matches a proper name before the word itself (Già → Gia, Sarà → Sara, Tornò → Torno), and from phrases (è poi → e poi → eppoi): with Yomitan's processor, 88 instead of 23 of the 233,208 lookups of five Gutenberg texts have a first result the dictionary's rows do not confirm (sources/measure.py text, wty-it-en as published).

Inputs that start with a combining mark, or hold the ångström sign (U+212B), which no Italian word does: the pack's pattern needs a letter before the mark it removes and writes the result in NFC (Å), where Yomitan removes every mark and leaves NFD.

The pack does not capitalise the article i: a step after the capital turns a final I back into i. wty-it-en has no entry for i, only form-of rows (il, la, lo, gli, le, l' and the letter I); the capitalised variant I finds the letter during the scan, and since ties go to the candidate found first (docs/languages.md 9.6), the letter came before il, which the plural rule reaches (i: 1,281,797 of it_50k's tokens).

A text that ends in a capital I (I, XVI, PAPI): the same step turns that I into i, which Yomitan's processor does not, so the pack also looks up XVi and PAPi, which no dictionary has; the variant i of I is also decapitalize's.
